title: Trump, Xi and Putin to Meet in Shenzhen on Nov. 19 in First-Ever Three-Way Talks
excerpt: President Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19, the White House confirmed, in a first-ever three-way meeting.
content:
President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19, the White House confirmed on Friday, November 13, in the first three-way meeting of the leaders of the world’s three largest nuclear powers.

The gathering will take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which China is hosting in Shenzhen, the southern Chinese technology hub, on November 18 and 19. The three leaders have met in pairs many times but have never held formal talks as a trio.

What is on the agenda

The White House said the meeting will focus on nuclear weapons. Spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters that Trump “will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous.”

A senior administration official who briefed reporters said Trump also intends to raise the war in Iran with both leaders. The same official said Russia’s war in Ukraine will not be discussed at the trilateral meeting at all.

Expectations are deliberately low. The senior official was blunt about what the session would produce: “We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement.” The meeting is instead described as an entry point — a first conversation that could, in time, lead to negotiations on a new arms-control framework between the three countries.

That context matters because the last treaty limiting the nuclear arsenals of the United States and Russia, New START, expired in February, leaving the world’s two largest nuclear powers without any binding cap on their arsenals for the first time in decades.

Still being negotiated

Beijing and Moscow had not formally confirmed their participation when the White House announcement landed on Friday, and planning was described as still in motion, with no format or venue details released. The agenda itself is still being negotiated in public: Washington wants nuclear arms and Iran on the table and Ukraine kept off it.

Trump leaves Washington on Monday, November 16, for a four-day Asia trip that begins in the Philippines. He is scheduled to meet Xi separately on Thursday afternoon for talks and a working lunch before the three-way gathering.

The APEC summit brings together 21 Pacific economies under the theme “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together,” with Xi chairing the meeting. The APEC CEO Summit runs November 17 and 18, ahead of the leaders’ meeting on November 18 and 19.

Why it matters in Laredo

For Webb County readers, the talks are not only about nuclear weapons. Laredo is the nation’s busiest inland port, and U.S.-China trade runs through this border every day. Decisions made in rooms like the one in Shenzhen shape tariffs, supply chains, and the flow of goods across the bridges here. Webb Watch 956 will report what, if anything, the three leaders agree to — or fail to agree to — when they sit down together.
